tutorials.title: Tour your workspace
tutorials.description: The board, brands, products, library, styles and rules: what each part of AutoCut is for.

steps.title: Your board
steps.body: Every ad your agency is working on is a card here, from To do to Done. Filter by person or brand at the top.

steps.title: Work moves left to right
steps.body: When an editor finishes an ad it moves to In review. Approving it sends it to Done; requesting changes sends it back.

steps.title: Start a new ad
steps.body: Every ad starts here. You pick the brand and product, and AutoCut walks you through the rest.

steps.title: Open Brands
steps.body: Click Brands to see your clients.

steps.title: One workspace per client
steps.body: Each brand keeps its own audience, products, recurring cast and provider keys, so clients never mix.

steps.title: Open Products
steps.body: Click Products.

steps.title: Everything you advertise
steps.body: Each product has its facts, size and reference photos. Generated images use them to get the product right.

steps.title: Open the Library
steps.body: Click Library.

steps.title: Your best work, reusable
steps.body: Save strong images and videos here and drop them into any future ad. Library items are never auto-deleted.

steps.title: Open Styles
steps.body: Click Styles.

steps.title: Looks you can pick
steps.body: A style is a visual look, like Creator UGC or Anatomy Glow. Every style shows a preview of what it produces.

steps.title: Open Rules
steps.body: Click Rules.

steps.title: AutoCut learns from feedback
steps.body: When your team gives the same feedback more than once, it becomes a rule, so the mistake isn't repeated in new ads.

steps.title: Notifications
steps.body: The bell tells you when something needs your review, was approved, or needs changes.

steps.title: Your profile
steps.body: Change your name and photo here, and switch between light and dark mode below. You're all set.

tutorials.title: Set up a client brand
tutorials.description: Add a brand and fill in the context that keeps every script and image on brand.

steps.title: Add a brand
steps.body: Click New brand to add a client.

steps.title: Name it
steps.body: Use the client's brand name. You can add a logo link below it.

steps.title: Who it speaks to
steps.body: Describe the buyer in a sentence or two. Scripts and hooks are written for this audience.

steps.title: How it sounds
steps.body: Warm, direct, playful: the voice every script is written in.

steps.title: Facts that must stay true
steps.body: Anything that must never be misstated, like ingredients, sizes or guarantees.

steps.title: How it looks
steps.body: Colours, light and mood. This steers every generated image.

steps.title: What the frame should contain
steps.body: Describe what should be in the shot instead of listing don'ts. Image models tend to draw whatever a 'no' list names.

steps.title: Claims rules
steps.body: What can and can't be claimed. Scripts follow this, which keeps ads compliant.

steps.title: Audience profiles
steps.body: Add the brand's buyer types, with their problems and the words they use. Scripts are written to them.

steps.title: Recurring characters
steps.body: The cast library keeps the same people looking the same across every ad for this brand.

steps.title: Brand keys
steps.body: A brand can use its own provider keys, so its AI costs are billed separately from your other clients.

tutorials.title: Add a product and photos
tutorials.description: Product facts, real size and reference photos: the three things that make generated images accurate.

steps.title: New product
steps.body: Add products here or from inside a brand.

steps.title: Open a product
steps.body: Click a product to see what it holds.

steps.title: What it is
steps.body: One clear line. Claude uses it in every script and image prompt for this product.

steps.title: Real size
steps.body: This keeps the product the right size next to hands and people in generated images.

steps.title: Reference photos
steps.body: Upload 3 or 4 clean photos from different angles, on a plain background. Every image of this product is generated from them.

steps.title: Its ads
steps.body: Every ad made for this product lives here, including archived ones.

tutorials.title: Make an ad, step by step
tutorials.description: From brief to export: scripts, scene plan, cast, storyboard, images, voiceover and videos.

steps.title: Create an ad
steps.body: Click Create ad.

steps.title: Pick the brand and product
steps.body: Choose the brand, then the product. Next you pick the ad's main style and AutoCut opens the ad.

steps.title: Every ad has these steps
steps.body: Here's a finished ad. Steps run left to right; once a step is done you can click back to it any time.

steps.title: 1. Scripts
steps.body: Set the length and Claude writes three script variants from the brand, audience and product. Pick one or regenerate.

steps.title: 2. Fine-tune the brief
steps.body: Tighten the hook, the offer and the tone before the script is split into scenes.

steps.title: 3. Scene plan
steps.body: The script becomes short scenes, each with its line. Split, merge or reorder them, then lock the plan.

steps.title: 4. Concept and cast
steps.body: Pick a creative concept and the people in it. Cast members keep the same face in every scene.

steps.title: 5. Storyboard
steps.body: Each scene gets a shot description and its own style. Claude can suggest the best style per scene.

steps.title: 6. Scene images
steps.body: Generate 1 to 4 images per scene and keep the best. You see the cost before anything runs.

steps.title: 7. Voiceover
steps.body: Record the script in a voice you choose, with captions timed to it.

steps.title: 8. Scene videos
steps.body: Each image becomes a short clip. Videos take a few minutes and keep running if you close the tab.

steps.title: 9. Export
steps.body: Download everything or pick exactly what you want, then finish the cut in your editing tool. That's the whole ad.

tutorials.title: Mix styles and ask Claude
tutorials.description: Give each scene its own look, let Claude suggest styles, and ask Claude to write a scene's image prompt.

steps.title: Let Claude suggest styles
steps.body: Claude reads every scene and suggests the best style for each, with a reason. Nothing changes until you apply it.

steps.title: A style per scene
steps.body: Each scene can have its own look, like a UGC hook, then a 3D anatomy cutaway, then a clean product shot. Click to change it.

steps.title: Pick by preview
steps.body: Every style shows what it looks like. Pick one for just this scene, or keep the ad's style.

steps.title: Ask Claude in plain words
steps.body: Say what a scene should show, like "scene 6 is the CTA, write a prompt for it". Claude writes it in that scene's style.

steps.title: See a scene's prompt
steps.body: Each scene card has its image prompt. Click Edit prompt.

steps.title: The prompt lands here
steps.body: Claude's prompt appears in this box. Edit it if you like, save, then regenerate the scene. Nothing is generated until you do.

tutorials.title: Review and approve
tutorials.description: How ads move through review, and how reviewers request changes scene by scene.

steps.title: Open a task in review
steps.body: Click a card in In review.

steps.title: Open the review
steps.body: A task in review links to its ad and review round. Review now opens it.

steps.title: Review scene by scene
steps.body: Approve each scene or flag it with a note. One click sends the whole review: everything approved moves the task to Done, any flag sends it back to Revisions.

steps.title: The editor sees exactly what to fix
steps.body: Flagged scenes come back highlighted, with the reviewer's note already in the feedback box.

tutorials.title: Invite your team
tutorials.description: Invite editors and admins, choose their role, and decide which brands they work on.

steps.title: Your team
steps.body: Everyone in your agency, their role and their brands.

steps.title: Invite by email
steps.body: Enter their work email. They get a sign-in link; if email is slow you can share a link instead.

steps.title: Pick a role
steps.body: Admins manage brands and see spend. Users work on the brands you assign them.

tutorials.title: Keys, spend and your plan
tutorials.description: Connect your AI providers, set spend limits, and see your plan's usage.

steps.title: Connect your providers
steps.body: AutoCut runs on your own AI keys, so you pay providers directly with no markup. Anthropic writes, kie.ai or fal.ai make images and video.

steps.title: Spend guard
steps.body: AutoCut tracks the last 24 hours of spend. It warns you at one limit and pauses generation at another, until an owner resumes it.

steps.title: Plan and usage
steps.body: Your plan, renewal date, and how many seats, brands and storage you're using.
